chunks: From him, from al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Ḥajjāj, who said:

I heard Ibn Abī Laylā saying: The blood-money in the Jāhiliyyah was one hundred camels, and the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله confirmed it. Then he imposed upon the people of cattle two hundred cows, and he imposed upon the people of sheep one thousand sheep, and upon the people of Yemen one hundred garments.

ʿAbd al-Raḥmān said: So I asked Abā ʿAbdillah عليه السلام about what was narrated from Ibn Abī Laylā, and he said: ‘ʿAlī عليه السلام used to say: The blood-money is one thousand dinars, and the value of the dinars is ten thousand dirhams. Upon the people of gold is one thousand dinars, and upon the people of silver is ten thousand dirhams for the people of the towns; for the people of the deserts, the blood-money is one hundred camels; and for the people of the Sawād, two hundred cows or one thousand sheep.’

key_terms.أَلْفُ دِينَارٍ: one thousand dinars; the stated dīyah amount for people of gold
key_terms.الدِّيَةُ: blood-money; the prescribed financial compensation for wrongful killing or bodily injury
key_terms.الْأَمْصَارِ: the settled towns and urban centers
key_terms.الْبَوَادِي: the desert-dwelling people or Bedouin regions
key_terms.الْجَاهِلِيَّةِ: the pre-Islamic period before the advent of Islam
key_terms.الْحُلَلَ: garments; a specified form of dīyah payment for the people of Yemen
key_terms.عَشَرَةُ آلَافِ دِرْهَمٍ: ten thousand dirhams; the equivalent valuation of the dīyah

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith say about the amount and forms of dīyah in Islamic law?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses the legal assessment of dīyah according to different economic conditions and customary forms of wealth. It cites what was attributed to Ibn Abī Laylā and then presents the ruling reported from Imam Jaʿfar al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام from أمير المؤمنين ʿAlī عليه السلام, detailing equivalent amounts in dinars, dirhams, camels, cows, and sheep.
